title: External professionals
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches economic externalities, which is unrelated to external professionals such as accountants and lawyers advising on legal duties.

draft.title: External professionals
card: External professionals are experts outside the business who give advice or services. The owner pays them for their time.
Helps with records, tax returns and GST, and can advise on the business's finances.
Advises on legal duties and checks documents such as leases and contracts.
A bank manager can advise on loans, and an insurance broker on cover. A business adviser can help plan the business.
draft.remember: External experts help an owner meet legal duties and set the business up well.

a.q: Sam is about to sign a five-year lease for a shop. He wants an expert to check the lease before he signs. Who should he ask?
a.why: A lawyer checks documents such as leases and contracts. An accountant is the tempting wrong answer, but accountants deal with records, tax and finances, not the legal terms of a lease.

b.q: Aisha's new florist in Ballarat is growing, and she is unsure how to keep her records and lodge her tax returns correctly. Who is best placed to help her?
b.why: An accountant helps with records, tax returns and GST. A lawyer advises on legal duties and documents, so it is the tempting wrong answer, but records and tax returns are the accountant's work.
b.clue: Which expert handles records and tax?
